extracted.intended_audience: poets, dramatists, and readers interested in aesthetic principles and creative writing
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and aesthetic principles for composing poetry and theatrical works rooted in truth, nature, passion, and sincere emotion, with warnings against artificiality and the domestication of poetic genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and fidelity to nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Art (especially theatre) should unite with truth and represent nature as it reveals itself; avoid fashionable, false rules and mannerisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "Nature we love when she her form reveals; Fashion's false rules no more are deified; 'Tis with truth only it can e'er unite, Its glow free spirits only e'er can light." (advocates grounding art in truth and natural representation rather than in artificial fashions)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and genuine emotion on stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatrical representation should be sincere: genuine feeling (a real tear) is the only thing true and affecting; affectation or simulated truth is a snare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "Nothing is true and genuine save--a tear; Emotion on no dream of sense relies. The real Melpomene is still sincere... By truth profound to charm us is her care; The false one, truth pretends, but to ensnare." (prioritizes authentic emotional expression over superficial fable)

rubrics_metrics.name: Passion combined with truth yields beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: The beautiful in art arises from passion that is wedded to truth; passion alone or artifice alone is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "'Tis passion makes the notes of freedom sound, And 'tis in truth the beautiful is found."

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid artificial, boastful gestures; favor living spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Styles full of boasting gestures and spurious pride lack a living spirit; art should be animated by genuine inner life rather than grandiose, empty mannerisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "For in his art no living spirit reigns: The boasting gestures of a spurious pride That mind which only loves the true disdains." (criticizes affected manner and urges authenticity)

rubrics_metrics.name: Native / national authenticity in theatre
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatre should spring from native art and genius rather than slavishly imitate foreign models or 'idols'; a culture's own sensibility should inform its dramatic art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "This theatre belongs to native art, No foreign idols worshipped here are seen; A laurel we can show, with joyous heart, That on the German Pindus has grown green... The German genius dares to enter e'en." (advocates local authenticity and self-derived inspiration)

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand the stage to encompass broader life and realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern theatre should widen its scope to include the universe of life — mingling the meanest and noblest — rather than confining itself to narrow, artificial subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "The narrow theatre is now more wide, Into its space a universe now steals... Now from the scene, art threatens to retire, Her kingdom wild maintains still phantasy; The stage she like the world would set on fire, The meanest and the noblest mingles she." (urges embracing life's breadth and realism on stage)

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of form, harmony of movement and dance
rubrics_metrics.description: On stage, physical movement, language, and form should join harmoniously; dance and measured motion lend grace and order to dramatic presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "To him e'en language rises into song; A realm harmonious 'tis, of beauty mild, Where limb unites to limb in order strong. The whole into a solemn temple blends, And 'tis the dance that grace to motion lends." (emphasizes formal harmony and the role of movement)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not domesticate or overwork poetic genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetic inspiration (the Pegasus) resists being clipped, yoked, or forced into purely utilitarian tasks; attempts to harness or starve creative genius will destroy its soaring nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary and lines from the narrative 'Pegasus in Harness': the hippogriff sold, clipped, yoked to oxen and driven to plough, wastes and is ruined; but when guided by a master-hand the creature soars again. (warning against domestication and misuse of poetic talent; suggests the necessity of proper guidance and conditions)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject confinement by archaic/formal rules; accept change
rubrics_metrics.description: Art should not bind itself to worn-out chains of convention; the new supersedes the old as time advances and art must evolve rather than nostalgically imitate past rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original lines: "'Tis not to bind us in a worn-out chain... The winged hours forever bear it on, The new arrives, and, lo! the old has gone." (advocates innovation over slavish adherence to outdated forms)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy should not rely solely on fools/simpletons
rubrics_metrics.description: Having many fools or simpletons is not the essence of comedy; true comedy requires craft beyond merely populating a play with buffoons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original line: "Fools we may have in plenty, and simpletons, too, by the dozen; But for comedy these never make use of themselves." (a caution about simplistic comic device)

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve youthful imagination and the ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet/artist should guard the imaginative, ideal life against becoming hardened by mere experience or cynical practicality; the ideal supplies hope and poetic vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages from 'THE POETRY OF LIFE' and related lines: contrasts the coldness of experience with the loss of 'godlike images' and urges not to surrender the dream/ideal path in life and art. (admonition to maintain imaginative vitality)
